title: Apply for land use (use-value) taxation
question: My land is farmed, forested or open space. How do I get it taxed at use value?
office: Department of Finance and Budget, County Assessor's Office (real estate assessment), acting for the Director of Finance
summary: Albemarle County can tax farm, horticultural, forest and open-space land on its use value instead of its market value. The tax difference is deferred, not forgiven. The use must be commercial and in place before January 1. Minimums are 5 acres for agriculture or horticulture and 20 acres for forest or open space, with homesites left out. Open space also needs an easement, a district or a county agreement. File one Use-Value Application per parcel with the County Assessor's Office, with production records and a $125 fee, at least 60 days before the tax year. Late filing costs $125 more. Enrolled land is revalidated every two years. Leaving the use triggers roll-back taxes. Appeal to the Assessor, then circuit court.

legal_basis.quote: Determine that the parcel is not in a planned development, or an industrial or commercial zoning district established prior to January 1, 1981, as referred to in Virginia Code § 58.1-3237.1.
The owner is liable for a penalty equal to 10 percent of the amount of the roll-back tax.

steps.step: Check that the land is in a qualifying use and meets the county's minimum acreage
steps.how: Albemarle offers use-value taxation for all four state classes: agriculture (crops or livestock produced mainly for sale), horticulture (fruit, nuts, berries, vineyards, nursery and floral products), forest, and open space. The county minimums are 5 cleared acres under use for agriculture, 5 acres for horticulture, 20 acres for forest and 20 acres for open space. Contiguous land titled in the same ownership is added together. The homesite, lawns, driveways, landscaped areas and non-farm buildings are left out. The county page says land under lakes and ponds is generally included but is not counted toward the 5-acre minimum (see caveats), and that cleared areas are not counted toward the 20-acre forest minimum. It adds that forest areas under 20 acres may qualify if the parcel first qualifies for agricultural or horticultural use. Horses kept for pleasure, and not in a commercial use such as boarding, breeding or training, do not qualify. Land in a planned development, or in an industrial or commercial zoning district created before January 1, 1981, is excluded.
steps.source: https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use (read from the Internet Archive copy of March 4, 2026, https://web.archive.org/web/20260304082651/https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use, because www.albemarle.org refuses automated requests)

steps.step: Make sure the qualifying use is established before January 1 of the year you apply
steps.how: The county wants a stable commercial operation in place before January 1 of the year you apply. It describes this as two or more years of production that meet the minimum standards. Agricultural and horticultural land must show at least $1,000 a year in revenue per parcel from the qualifying use. Every category must follow best management practices to protect soil and water. A past use that has stopped does not count.
steps.deadline: before January 1 of the application year
steps.source: https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use/apply-for-land-use (read from the Internet Archive copy of April 17, 2026, https://web.archive.org/web/20260417123736/https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use/apply-for-land-use, because www.albemarle.org refuses automated requests)

steps.step: For forest or open-space land, get the extra document the category needs
steps.who: Property owner; a professional forester (forest plan); a public body or the County (easement, district or agreement)
steps.how: Forest land needs a forest management plan prepared by a professional forester, or the owner's own signed written commitment to manage and protect the forest. You must intend to harvest timber at some point, and no deed restriction may forbid it. Open-space land must be under a conservation easement held by a public body, be in an Agricultural or Forestal District, or be under an Open Space Use Agreement with the County (a recorded commitment for 4 to 10 years). It must also be consistent with the County's land use plan. Land in a district or under an agreement may not qualify if it keeps no unused development rights.
steps.source: https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use (read from the Internet Archive copy of March 4, 2026, https://web.archive.org/web/20260304082651/https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use, because www.albemarle.org refuses automated requests)

steps.step: Pay any delinquent taxes on the parcel before you apply
steps.who: Property owner; Office of Revenue Administration (tax payments)
steps.how: An application cannot be accepted or approved while the tax on the land is delinquent. Pay all delinquent taxes, penalties and interest first. The state model application form also says it will not be accepted if taxes on the parcel are delinquent.
steps.quote: Except as provided by local ordinance, no application for assessment based on use shall be accepted or approved if, at the time the application is filed, the tax on the land affected is delinquent.

steps.step: Gather proof of the qualifying use
steps.how: Fill in the animal and crop production tables on the application, or attach records. Examples are IRS Schedule F (farm profit or loss), Form 4835 (farm rental income), Schedule E, Schedule C, Form 1120 or Form 1065, farm sales receipts, or a farm or forest management plan. The records must show a commercial operation. If you lease the land to a farmer, the county may not require a copy of the lease.
steps.source: https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use/apply-for-land-use (read from the Internet Archive copy of April 17, 2026, https://web.archive.org/web/20260417123736/https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use/apply-for-land-use, because www.albemarle.org refuses automated requests)

steps.step: Complete one Use-Value Application for each parcel
steps.who: Property owner (all owners of an interest in the parcel should sign)
steps.how: Use the county's Use-Value Application, one for each tax parcel. The state model form (LU-1) lets several qualifying uses on the same parcel go on one application, and it treats a missing signature of any owner of an interest as a material misstatement, so have all owners sign. The county's own form was not read. An owner of an undivided interest may apply for the others only with an affidavit that they are minors, cannot be found, or hold a minority interest. Wrong information about the owners or the use, or an intentionally wrong acreage, is a material misstatement. It voids the use-value assessment and makes the full taxes due.
steps.quote: A separate application must be filed for each tax parcel.

steps.step: File the application with the $125 fee by the deadline
steps.who: Property owner; County Assessor's Office (receives the application); Director of Finance (receives the fee)
steps.how: Submit the application, the supporting documents and the $125 fee to the County Assessor's Office. The Apply page gives its address as 401 McIntire Rd, Room 243, Charlottesville, VA 22902. The pages read do not say whether the application may be mailed, emailed or faxed, or how the fee is paid; the ordinance says the fee is paid to the Director of Finance. State law requires filing at least 60 days before the tax year, which starts January 1. The county page gives November 1 of the year before, but it still shows the 2025 tax year (November 1, 2024). An application without the required information or fee counts as not filed. Application fees are not refunded.
steps.deadline: at least 60 days preceding the tax year (Va. Code § 58.1-3234(1)); the county page says November 1 (for the 2025 tax year, November 1, 2024)
steps.source: https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use/apply-for-land-use (read from the Internet Archive copy of April 17, 2026, https://web.archive.org/web/20260417123736/https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use/apply-for-land-use, because www.albemarle.org refuses automated requests)

steps.step: If you miss the deadline, file late with a late fee
steps.how: The ordinance allows filing up to 60 days after the state deadline with a $125 late fee, so $250 in all. The county page gives the late window as November 2 through December 31. After that the parcel cannot be taxed at use value for that tax year, unless the 30-day window after the January assessment notice applies (step s9).
steps.deadline: no later than 60 days after the filing deadline (county page: November 2 through December 31)
steps.fee: $125.00 late filing fee on top of the $125.00 application fee ($250.00 in all)
steps.quote: An application may be filed no later than 60 days after the filing deadline specified in Virginia Code § 58.1-3234, upon the payment of a late filing fee of $125.00.

steps.step: New parcel or higher assessment: use the 30-day window after the January notice
steps.how: If the parcel is new for the tax year, or its assessment went up on the Notice of Assessment mailed in January, you may apply within 30 days from that notice's date. Albemarle reassesses every year and mails notices by the end of January.
steps.deadline: inside 30 days of that notice's date
steps.fee: Not stated for this window (the application fee is $125.00)
steps.source: https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use/apply-for-land-use (read from the Internet Archive copy of April 17, 2026, https://web.archive.org/web/20260417123736/https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use/apply-for-land-use, because www.albemarle.org refuses automated requests)

steps.step: The County Assessor's Office reviews the application
steps.who: County Assessor's Office, for the Director of Finance (the local assessing officer)
steps.how: The office checks that the land meets the state standards for its class and the minimum acreage, and decides which areas qualify, leaving out homesites. It also checks that the zoning exclusion does not apply. It may ask for proof of ownership, acreage, use and production. In unclear cases it may ask the Virginia Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, the State Forester or the Department of Conservation and Recreation for an opinion. No source sets a time limit for the decision.
steps.quote: Before assessing a parcel under this article, the Director of Finance (or his designee) shall make all determinations required under Virginia Code § 58.1-3233

steps.step: If approved, the land is taxed at its use value
steps.who: County Assessor's Office (valuation); Office of Revenue Administration (billing and payment)
steps.how: The qualifying land is valued only for its farm, forest or open-space use, taking into account the State Land Evaluation Advisory Council's recommendations. The house, homesite and other unrelated structures are valued at market value. The land book records both values. The tax difference is deferred, not forgiven. Real estate tax is billed in two halves, due June 25 and December 5 (the next business day if that falls on a weekend).
steps.quote: the commissioner of the revenue or duly appointed assessor shall consider only those indicia of value which such real estate has for agricultural, horticultural, forest or open space use

steps.who: Property owner; County Assessor's Office (mails the forms and runs compliance checks)
steps.how: The County mails revalidation forms, tailored to each parcel's prior use, to owners of enrolled parcels. For the 2026 cycle the staff report set June 18, 2025 as the target date for mailing them, and an optional online system was added. File one form per parcel by September 1 of the year before the two-year period. Late forms are accepted through December 5 with a $125 late fee per parcel. A parcel not revalidated by December 5 is removed from the program for the next tax year. Roll-back tax is assessed only if the use has actually stopped. Staff then check compliance using aerial imagery and, where needed, a field visit.
steps.deadline: on or before September 1 of the year preceding the two-year period; late filing through December 5
steps.fee: None if filed on time; $125.00 per parcel late fee
steps.quote: The owner must file a revalidation form with the local assessing officer on or before September 1 of the year preceding the two-year period for which the revalidation is sought, on forms prepared by the County.

steps.step: Report any change in use or acreage
steps.how: Tell the County Assessor's Office if the land changes to another qualifying use or to a non-qualifying use, or if the acreage changes (for example when a lot is sold or split off). A new application is needed when the approved use or acreage changes. No application fee is due when only the use changes to another qualifying use. Failing to report a change adds a 10 percent penalty to the roll-back tax.
steps.deadline: within sixty days following such change in use or zoning (state law); the county page says immediately
steps.fee: No application fee when only the use changes to another qualifying use (County Code § 15-715(B)), or when the acreage changes only because of a conveyance forced by governmental action or condemnation (Va. Code § 58.1-3234); 10 percent penalty on the roll-back tax for failing to report
steps.quote: shall, within sixty days following such change in use or zoning, report such change to the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing officer on such forms as may be prescribed.

steps.step: Keep the real estate taxes paid
steps.who: Property owner; Director of Finance (acting as treasurer and commissioner of the revenue)
steps.how: If taxes for any prior year on the parcel are delinquent on April 1, the County must send a notice by first-class mail. If they are still unpaid on June 1, the parcel is removed from the program for the current tax year. A parcel is not removed if the taxes became delinquent during a state of emergency declared by the Governor, the treasurer (in Albemarle, the Director of Finance) determines that the disaster caused hardship, and the taxes are paid within 90 days after the June 1 deadline.
steps.deadline: Delinquent taxes still unpaid on June 1 lead to removal
steps.quote: If, after the notice has been sent, such delinquent taxes remain unpaid on June 1, the treasurer shall notify the appropriate commissioner of the revenue who shall remove such parcel from the land use program.

steps.step: Pay roll-back taxes if the land leaves a qualifying use
steps.who: Owner at the time of the change; Director of Finance (assesses and collects)
steps.how: Roll-back tax falls on the part of the land affected when it changes to a non-qualifying use, is rezoned to a more intensive use at the owner's request, or is split off as a lot (a split that leaves parcels meeting the minimum acreage and still in a qualifying use does not trigger it). It equals the deferred taxes for the five most recent complete tax years plus interest, and the current year is taxed at market value. The county estimates this at about 6.5 to 8 times the annual tax. It says a homesite of at least two acres is rolled back when a permit is taken out to build a new home. Payment is due within 30 days. After that a further 10 percent penalty and 10 percent yearly interest apply. A sale alone does not trigger roll-back if the new owner keeps the qualifying use.
steps.deadline: within 30 days after the date of assessment
steps.fee: Roll-back tax (five years of deferred tax plus interest); 10 percent penalty plus 10 percent yearly interest if paid late
steps.quote: The owner must pay the roll-back tax plus interest and any penalty within 30 days after the date of assessment.

escalation.next: Director of Finance (the assessing official with the commissioner of the revenue's powers): a written application to correct an erroneous assessment
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later (Va. Code § 58.1-3980(A)). An error in valuing land subject to roll-back tax may be corrected within three years of the roll-back assessment (Va. Code § 58.1-3981(D)).
escalation.quote: Sections 58.1-3980 through 58.1-3983 shall also apply to erroneous assessments of real estate if the error sought to be corrected in any case was made by the commissioner of the revenue or such other official to whom the application is made

escalation.trigger: The Director acts on the correction request and you want the reasons in writing
escalation.next: Director of Finance: a written statement of the facts and law behind the decision, on request
escalation.quote: if so requested by the applicant, the commissioner or other such official shall state in writing the facts and law supporting the action on such application and mail a copy of such writing to the applicant at his last known address.

escalation.trigger: The County Assessor has ruled on qualification and you still disagree (the county's Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights page adds that a taxpayer can appeal to the circuit court at any stage of the administrative review)
escalation.next: Circuit Court of Albemarle County: an application for relief from an erroneous assessment
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, one year from the assessment, or one year from the final determination under Va. Code § 58.1-3981, whichever is later (Va. Code § 58.1-3984(A))
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3984(A); county Apply for Use-Value Program page (Circuit Court once the Assessor has ruled, https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/land-use/apply-for-land-use, Internet Archive copy of April 17, 2026); county Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights page (court at any point, https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance-and-budget/business/notice-of-taxpayer-appeal-rights, Internet Archive copy of March 11, 2026)
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made

escalation.trigger: It is unclear whether the land meets the state standards for its class
escalation.next: Commissioner of Agriculture and Consumer Services, State Forester or Director of the Department of Conservation and Recreation: an opinion requested by the assessing officer (an owner can only ask the office to request one)
escalation.quote: Determine that the real estate meets the criteria set forth in § 58.1-3230 and the standards prescribed thereunder to qualify for one of the classifications set forth therein, and he may request an opinion from the Director of the Department of Conservation and Recreation, the State Forester or the Commissioner of Agriculture and Consumer Services;

escalation.trigger: The state official refuses to give an opinion, or gives an unfavorable opinion that does not follow the published standards
escalation.next: Circuit Court of Albemarle County: relief, which may include an order in place of the opinion
escalation.quote: the party aggrieved may seek relief in the circuit court of the county or city wherein the real estate in question is located

escalation.trigger: The land qualifies, but you think its use value or market value is wrong (a value question, not qualification)
escalation.next: County Assessor's review, then the Albemarle County Board of Equalization (which cannot decide land use qualification)
escalation.deadline: 2026 dates on the county page: Assessor's review requested by March 2, 2026; Board of Equalization application by March 30, 2026, or within 30 days of the Assessor's review letter, whichever is later. The 2027 dates were not found in the copies read.
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3243; https://www.albemarle.org/government/finance/real-estate-tax-assessments (Internet Archive copy of August 14, 2026)
escalation.quote: including, without limitation, provisions relating to tax liens, boards of equalization and the correction of erroneous assessments

escalation.trigger: Taxes became delinquent during a state of emergency declared by the Governor and the parcel faces removal
escalation.next: Director of Finance (acting as treasurer): finding that the disaster caused hardship, so the parcel stays in the program
escalation.deadline: Delinquent taxes paid no later than 90 days after the June 1 deadline
escalation.quote: No parcel of real property shall be removed from the land use program for delinquent taxes if (i) the taxes become delinquent during a state of emergency declared by the Governor

escalation.trigger: No complete application with the fee was filed by the late-filing deadline
escalation.next: File a new application for the next tax year (no route was found for accepting a filing after the late deadline)
escalation.deadline: At least 60 days before the next tax year (county page: November 1)
escalation.quote: Failure to file a complete application by the deadlines in subsections (A) or (D) disqualifies the entire tax parcel for taxation under this article.

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The Apply page's deadline text is the same in its copies of November 2, 2025, January 18, 2026 and April 10, 2026. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act.

Stale dates: the Apply page still gives the dates for the 2025 tax year (November 1, 2024, and a late window of November 2 to December 31, 2024). No page read gives the dates for the 2027 tax year. Under state law and the ordinance, a new application is due at least 60 days before January 1, 2027. On the county's past pattern that is November 1, 2026, which is a Sunday. The county moves tax payment due dates that fall on a weekend to the next business day, but no source says this applies to land use applications. As of 2026-10-11, file early or ask the office.

The Use-Value Application itself (https://www.albemarle.org/home/showdocument?id=19783&t=638356605841105031) was not archived and could not be read. Not known: its contents beyond the 'Animal/Crop production tables' the Land Use page mentions, whether it is fillable, how to pay the $125 fee (check, card or online), and whether it can be emailed or faxed.

County Code text comes from Ordinance No. 19-15(1), adopted 6:0 on April 17, 2019. It is Attachment 11 of the Board of Supervisors Actions document on albemarle.legistar.com. Legistar title searches (use value, land preservation, revalidation, 15-71, and every Chapter 15 matter since May 2019) found no later amendment to §§ 15-713 to 15-718. The only related item was a 2021 ordinance waiving the 2021 late revalidation fee for forms filed from September 1 to October 1, 2021, a one-time measure. An amendment whose title does not name these sections would have been missed. The current codified text on Municode has not been checked, because Municode's terms bar automated access. Read it at https://library.municode.com/va/albemarle_county/codes/code_of_ordinances.

Drafting slip in the ordinance: § 15-713 says the four use terms have the meanings 'defined in Virginia Code § 58.1-3210'. That section is the elderly and disabled tax relief statute. The definitions are in § 58.1-3230, which the ordinance's own state law reference names. The quote is kept word for word.

§ 15-715(B) also waives the application fee 'when only the use of a previously' approved parcel 'changes to another qualifying use'. The PDF breaks the line at a hyphen, so the exact spelling of 'previously-approved' is uncertain. That clause is paraphrased in the fee entry and in step s13, not quoted. Also, § 15-717's second subsection is printed '4B', read here as (B). § 15-716(C)(3) is quoted with its typo, 'revalidation from' for 'revalidation form'.

$1,000 minimum and history of use: the county pages require agricultural and horticultural land to show at least $1,000 a year in revenue per parcel. They also ask for 'two or more years of production' as a stabilized operation before January 1. The state standards in 2VAC5-20 (amended October 15, 2020) set no dollar minimum and no history period, and a text search of the SLEAC manual found no $1,000 figure. Va. Code § 58.1-3231 requires a shorter period, based on a written statement of intent, if the state standards ever set one. The county's figures look like local administrative practice, possibly stricter than state law. Ask the office before relying on them.

Open space: Albemarle requires 20 acres (County Code § 15-717(A)(4)), above the state default of 5 acres, as § 58.1-3233(2) allows. The county page names three ways to qualify: a conservation easement with a public body, an Agricultural or Forestal District, or an Open Space Use Agreement with the County. Enrolling in a district and signing an agreement are separate processes, not covered here. The county's agreement form was not found. The DCR form of agreement (4VAC5-20-30) is listed instead. The page also says land in a district or under an agreement without unused development rights will not qualify. That 'new rules' policy was not traced to an ordinance.

Revalidation: the ordinance requires revalidation every two years, by September 1 of the year before the two-year period, with late filing through December 5. The 2026 cycle followed this: forms targeted for mailing on June 18, 2025 (the staff report gives it as a target date, not as done), due September 1, 2025, late through December 5, 2025, per the staff report for Legistar file 25-294. By inference the next cycle covers 2028 and 2029, with forms due September 1, 2027, but no source states this. The URL of the online revalidation system was not found. The sample revalidation letter and forms (Attachment B to file 25-294) have not been checked.

Escalation is partly inferred. Neither Article 4 of Chapter 32 of Title 58.1 nor County Code Division 3 sets an appeal route for a denied application. The county Apply page gives the route: the County Assessor, then circuit court. It adds that the Board of Equalization decides value but not qualification, and that the office cannot advise on court appeals. Va. Code § 58.1-3243 applies the equalization and correction-of-assessment provisions of Title 58.1. The correction and circuit court rungs follow those provisions (§§ 58.1-3980, 58.1-3981, 58.1-3984), with the Director of Finance holding the commissioner of the revenue's powers (§ 15.2-521). No source sets a deadline for the Assessor to decide an application or an appeal. Circuit court filing fees are not covered here.

Advisory opinions: § 58.1-3233(1) and 2VAC5-20-40(B) let the assessing officer, not the owner, ask the state agencies for an opinion. Whether Albemarle's office will do so when an owner asks is not stated.

Delinquent taxes: as far as the 2019 text shows, County Code Division 3 does not adopt the option in § 58.1-3235(B) to keep a parcel in the program if delinquent taxes are paid by December 31. So the state rule applies: removal if the taxes are still unpaid on June 1. In Albemarle the Director of Finance holds both the treasurer's and the commissioner of the revenue's roles.

Roll-back: the Apply page speaks of 'the past five years' and the staff report of 'the current and five previous years'. State law sets the five most recent complete tax years plus the current year at market value (§ 58.1-3237(B)). The page's rule that a homesite of at least two acres is rolled back when a building permit is taken out is stated county practice. No ordinance text for it was found. Division 3 sets no interest rate for the interest built into the roll-back itself (§ 58.1-3237(B) leaves it to the governing body). County Code § 15-104, in the same 2019 ordinance, applies interest of 10 percent a year to all unpaid taxes and penalties from the month after they are due; whether it is the rate used for the interest built into the roll-back is not stated. The 2019 ordinance repealed the old County Code § 15-806 (roll-back taxes), so § 58.1-3237 governs the roll-back itself.

Ponds and lakes: the county page says land under lakes and ponds is generally included as agricultural or horticultural land but is not counted toward the five-acre minimum. Va. Code § 58.1-3236(B) says the area under ponds, lakes, streams and like facilities shall be included in determining the total area actively devoted to the use. Whether the county's minimum-acreage practice fits that rule was not resolved; ask the office if a pond decides whether the parcel reaches five acres.
Valuation: no page read states the per-acre use values Albemarle applies, or whether it adopts SLEAC's recommended values. § 58.1-3236(A) requires the assessor only to consider them.

Va. Code § 58.1-3234.1 takes effect January 1, 2027 (2026 Acts, cc. 308 and 309, as indexed). It requires the Department of Taxation to make a written notice form telling purchasers they can ask the assessor about use-value status and roll-back liability. How the notice will be delivered was not checked.

Agricultural and forestal districts: land in a district created under Chapter 43 of Title 15.2 is eligible even without a local ordinance (§§ 58.1-3231, 15.2-4312). Albemarle has an ordinance, so this matters mainly for the open-space route. It is assumed, not stated, that district land still needs the county application.

Va. Code § 58.1-3229 (the start of the article) is not in Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia, so it is not quoted. State-law quotes keep that copy's spacing before punctuation after cross-references (for example '§ 58.1-3230 .'). Regulations are quoted from law.lis.virginia.gov.

Contacts: the Land Use page displays 'Landuse@albemarle.org', but the link opens CountyAssessor@albemarle.org. Both are recorded as office mailboxes. The Legistar staff report names staff and lists a staff mailbox, and the Circuit Court Clerk page links a personal mailbox and names the clerks. None of these are recorded.
albemarle.org's terms allow browsing for information but forbid reposting its content without written permission. County page quotes are kept to one sentence or clause for citation.
The Legistar web page for file 25-294 (LegislationDetail.aspx) answers 'Invalid parameters!', so the staff report is cited by its Legistar Web API address.

The Internet Archive holds no copy of the Apply page later than April 17, 2026, none of the Land Use page later than March 4, 2026, and none of the Use-Value Application PDF, so the county's dates for the 2027 tax year are not confirmed. A Legistar title search of matters since May 2019 (Chapter 15, land use, use value, revalidation) found no amendment to §§ 15-713 to 15-718; the 2020 emergency ordinance amending Chapter 15 (file 20-261) has no text in Legistar and has not been checked.

corrections: Quotes: all 105 original quotes were re-checked. The 55 state-law quotes match I.text_of for the cited sections. The 50 others were matched word for word, with whitespace normalised, against fresh reads: the Ordinance 19-15(1) PDF on albemarle.legistar.com (text extracted as UTF-8, so the curly apostrophes in § 15-716 match), the Legistar Web API text of file 25-294, the seven law.lis.virginia.gov VAC pages, and the Internet Archive copies of the Land Use page (March 4, 2026) and the Apply page (April 17, 2026). lexflow's own check_quotes gives 57 of 57 code quotes matched after the additions below.

legal_basis: added two state-law entries, each copied from I.text_of: the § 58.1-3234 bar on an application fee when acreage changes only because of a conveyance forced by governmental action or condemnation, and the § 58.1-3241(B)(1) exception for splits that leave parcels meeting the minimum acreage in a qualifying use.

s1: the step said flatly that ponds do not count toward the 5-acre minimum. It now says this is the county page's statement, and a caveat notes the tension with § 58.1-3236(B). Also added two points from the Land Use page: cleared areas are not counted toward the 20-acre forest minimum, and forest under 20 acres may qualify if the parcel first qualifies for agricultural or horticultural use. The pleasure-horse exclusion now includes the page's commercial-use qualifier.
s6: 'All owners should sign' and 'several uses on one application' come from the state model form LU-1 in the SLEAC manual, not from the county's own form, which was not read. The step now says so.
s7: 'Deliver or mail' was not stated on any page read. The step now gives the Apply page's office address and says that the pages read do not state the delivery method or how to pay the fee.

s8: added that the 30-day window after the January assessment notice (s9) is still open after the late-filing window, since § 15-715(F) refers to the § 58.1-3234 deadline, and that deadline includes the reassessment window.
s12 and the revalidation caveat: the staff report gives June 18, 2025 only as the target date for mailing the forms, not as the date they were mailed. Reworded.
s13: the fee now also includes the state-law bar on an application fee for acreage changes caused by governmental action or condemnation.

s14: § 58.1-3235(C) leaves the hardship finding to the treasurer, not to 'the County'. The step now names the treasurer, who in Albemarle is the Director of Finance (County Code § 15-100(B)). The deadline now follows the statute: taxes still unpaid on June 1 lead to removal.
s15: added the § 58.1-3241(B)(1) exception, so that not every split-off triggers roll-back.

Escalation rung 4 (Circuit Court): the 'court at any point in the administrative process' statement is on the county's Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights page, not the Apply page. The trigger and basis now cite each page for what it says.
Escalation rung 7 (Board of Equalization): noted that the dates given are for 2026, and the 2027 dates were not found.
Contacts: moved the explanatory note about Landuse@albemarle.org out of the value field and into the label, so the value is a clean office mailbox.

Caveats: added the ponds caveat and the verification re-read caveat. The roll-back interest caveat now quotes the content of § 15-104 from the same ordinance and notes that the old § 15-806 was repealed. Added the Internet Archive capture index to sources.
open_issues: www.albemarle.org refuses automated requests (HTTP 403, robots.txt included). Every county page was checked against Internet Archive copies (Land Use, March 4, 2026; Apply, April 17, 2026; Real Estate Tax Assessments, August 14, 2026; Taxpayer Appeal Rights, March 11, 2026; Circuit Court Clerk, May 9, 2026; Terms, July 20, 2026), not against the live site. state-backbone.json says no third-party copies were quoted, so this method of quoting through Internet Archive copies still needs the user's confirmation. Sibling Albemarle files verified the same way.

The county's own dates for the 2027 tax year (new applications, about November 1, 2026, a Sunday) are not on any copy read. The steps give the state-law rule and the stale 2025 dates, with a caveat to file early.
The Use-Value Application PDF (showdocument?id=19783) was neither archived nor readable. Its fields, its signature rules, how the fee is paid, and whether it can be emailed or faxed are unknown.

The County Code was read as adopted in Ordinance 19-15(1) (2019). The current codified text on Municode was not read, under Municode's terms. No later amendment to §§ 15-713 to 15-718 was found by title search. The 2020 emergency Chapter 15 ordinance (file 20-261) has no API text.
The county's practice of not counting ponds toward the five-acre minimum may conflict with Va. Code § 58.1-3236(B). It is reported as the county's statement, not resolved.
